data.name: AgentRunner async loop with cancellation wiring
data.prompt: Extend crates/harness-runtime/src/agent_runner.rs with AgentRunner { agent: Agent, task: AgentTask, backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>, tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>, event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink>, agent_sequence: u64 }. Implement async fn run(&mut self) looping: receive AgentCommand from task.commands; call agent.apply(command) (pure/sync); for each AgentEffect dispatch: ExecuteBackend spawns backend.execute() in a tokio task forwarding ExecutionEvents back as AgentCommand::BackendEvent; ExecuteTool spawns tool_registry lookup + executor.execute() forwarding as AgentCommand::ToolCompleted/ToolFailed; Emit wraps AgentEvent into AgentEventEnvelope (agent_sequence++, session_id, agent_id, run_id, timestamp) sent via event_sink; FinishRun sends Completed event and breaks; CancelBackend/CancelTool/CancelChild delegate cancellation; SpawnAgent/RequestPermission/Persist are stubbed as no-op with a warning log for Phase 2. Create crates/harness-runtime/src/cancellation.rs with SessionCancellation { root: CancellationToken } exposing new(), child_token(), cancel(), is_cancelled(). AgentRunner derives its own child_token from the session root token and passes it into every backend/tool call; on cancellation it checks cancel.is_cancelled() before processing each command, sends AgentCommand::Cancel to the agent, drains resulting effects, emits StateChanged/Completed(Cancelled) events, and discards stale backend events for completed/cancelled runs by checking agent.state.active_run. Add tests: (1) FakeBackend scripted to emit a text delta then complete drives StartRun to Completed with expected ordered events; (2) a blocking FakeBackend call cancelled mid-flight causes transition to Cancelled and stops further backend events. harness-core remains untouched by async/tokio.

    Self::with_capacities(id, COMMAND_CAPACITY, EVENT_CAPACITY)

`AgentTask::new` takes **1 argument** (`id: AgentId`). The call site passes **3 arguments**. The 3-argument variant is `with_capacities(id, command_capacity, event_capacity)`. **This will not compile.**

### Issue 5 — `SessionRuntime.state.status` remains `Idle` forever

**File:** `crates/harness-runtime/src/session_runtime.rs`

`SessionRuntime::new` sets `status: SessionStatus::Idle` in the initial `SessionState`. But `send_command()` only forwards the `AgentCommand` to the root agent's task channel — it never updates `self.state.status`.

The `SessionEventBus::run` loop assigns `session_sequence` but doesn't feed state changes back into `SessionRuntime.state.status`.

//! Runtime executor that drives a single agent's lifecycle by receiving
//! [`AgentCommand`]s from its caller and publishing [`AgentEventEnvelope`]s
//! onto a session-level broadcast channel.
//!
//! The core primitive is [`AgentTask`] — the mailbox for one agent.

use tokio::sync::broadcast;
use tokio::sync::mpsc;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_protocol::commands::AgentCommand;
use harness_protocol::events::AgentEventEnvelope;
use harness_protocol::ids::AgentId;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentTask — mailbox primitive
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The mailbox and control handles for a single agent.
///
/// Every agent in the system is driven through an [`AgentTask`]:
///
/// | Field      | Purpose                                                    |
/// |------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
/// | `id`       | Stable [`AgentId`] that identifies this agent              |
/// | `commands` | Receiver half of an `mpsc` channel — the stream of         |
/// |            | [`AgentCommand`]s that the agent's run loop processes      |
/// | `events`   | Sender half of a `broadcast` channel — events produced by  |
/// |            | this agent are published here for the session to fan out   |
/// | `cancel`   | A [`CancellationToken`] that signals when this agent's     |
/// |            | work should be aborted                                     |
pub struct AgentTask {
    pub id: AgentId,
    pub commands: mpsc::Receiver<AgentCommand>,
    pub events: broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>,
    pub cancel: CancellationToken,
}

impl AgentTask {
    /// Create a new [`AgentTask`] together with a [`mpsc::Sender`] handle.
    ///
    /// The caller keeps the sender to push commands into the agent's mailbox;
    /// the returned [`AgentTask`] is consumed by the agent's run loop.
    ///
    /// # Channel capacity
    ///
    /// The command channel is buffered up to 64 items. The broadcast event
    /// channel holds 256 events before the oldest are dropped for slow readers.
    pub fn new(id: AgentId) -> (Self, mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>) {
        let (cmd_tx, cmd_rx) = mpsc::channel(64);
        let (evt_tx, _) = broadcast::channel(256);
        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();

        let task = Self {
            id,
            commands: cmd_rx,
            events: evt_tx,
            cancel,
        };

        (task, cmd_tx)
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Verify that a command sent through the sender is received on the
    /// receiver.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn send_command_through_mailbox() {
        let id = AgentId::new();
        let (mut task, tx) = AgentTask::new(id);

        let cmd = AgentCommand::Cancel;
        tx.send(cmd.clone()).await.expect("send command");

        let received = task.commands.recv().await.expect("receive command");
        assert_eq!(
            std::mem::discriminant(&cmd),
            std::mem::discriminant(&received),
            "the sent and received commands should have the same discriminant"
        );
    }
}

//! Core runtime traits for execution backends, tool executors, tool registries,
//! and event sinks.
//!
//! These are the **behavioral** traits that give life to the wire-format types
//! defined in [`harness-protocol`].  The protocol crate holds only serializable
//! data structures ([`ExecutionRequest`], [`ExecutionEvent`], [`ToolCall`],
//! [`AgentEventEnvelope`], etc.); the traits here drive the actual async I/O,
//! cancellation, and streaming that implement those contracts.

use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use tokio::sync::broadcast;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_protocol::backend::{
    BackendCapabilities, BackendDescriptor, ExecutionError, ExecutionEvent, ExecutionRequest,
    ExecutionResult,
};
use harness_protocol::events::AgentEventEnvelope;
use harness_protocol::tools::{ToolCall, ToolDescriptor, ToolError, ToolResult};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ExecutionBackend
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// An execution backend that processes agent requests against a language model.
///
/// Implementations wrap a specific provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) and are
/// responsible for:
///
/// * Serializing the [`ExecutionRequest`] into the provider's wire format.
/// * Streaming back normalized [`ExecutionEvent`]s (text deltas, reasoning,
///   tool call requests, usage updates, final result, or errors).
/// * Observing the [`CancellationToken`] so that in-flight requests can be
///   aborted promptly.
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible — all methods take `&self` and return owned
/// values or futures.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ExecutionBackend: Send + Sync {
    /// Returns the backend's descriptor, including its identity and capabilities.
    fn descriptor(&self) -> BackendDescriptor;

    /// Returns a summary of the backend's capabilities.
    fn capabilities(&self) -> BackendCapabilities;

    /// Execute a request against this backend.
    ///
    /// The backend streams [`ExecutionEvent`]s into `sink` as they occur
    /// and returns the final [`ExecutionResult`] once execution completes
    /// (or an [`ExecutionError`] if something went wrong).
    ///
    /// # Cancellation
    ///
    /// When `cancel` is triggered the backend should stop work as soon as
    /// practical and return [`ExecutionError::Cancelled`].
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        request: ExecutionRequest,
        sink: broadcast::Sender<ExecutionEvent>,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult, ExecutionError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ToolExecutor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Executes a single tool call and produces a result.
///
/// Each tool (e.g. `fs.read`, `bash`, `web_search`) is represented by an
/// implementation of this trait.  Tools are stateless from the harness's
/// perspective — any state they need should be captured at construction time
/// and stored in the implementor.
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolExecutor: Send + Sync {
    /// Execute the given tool call and return its result.
    ///
    /// # Cancellation
    ///
    /// When `cancel` is triggered the tool should stop work as soon as
    /// practical and return [`ToolError::Timeout`].
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        call: ToolCall,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ToolResult, ToolError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ToolRegistry
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A registry of available tool executors, indexed by tool name.
///
/// The harness uses this trait to look up tools when processing
/// [`ExecutionEvent::ToolCallRequested`] events.  Registries may be
/// session-scoped (containing only the tools granted to that session) or
/// global (containing every tool the runtime knows about).
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolRegistry: Send + Sync {
    /// Look up a tool executor by its name (e.g. `"fs.read"`).
    ///
    /// Returns `None` if no tool with that name is registered.
    fn lookup(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>;

    fn descriptors(&self) -> Vec<ToolDescriptor>;

/// A sink for receiving agent event envelopes.
///
/// Implementations are responsible for fanning events out to session-level
/// subscribers, persisting them, or forwarding them to external observers.
/// The canonical implementation publishes onto a
/// [`broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>`] but custom sinks may layer on
/// filtering, encryption, or audit logging.
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible.
#[async_trait]
pub trait EventSink: Send + Sync {
    /// Send an event envelope for processing.
    ///
    /// Implementations **should not** block indefinitely; if the underlying
    /// channel is full the implementation should decide whether to drop the
    /// event, buffer it, or apply backpressure.
    fn send(&self, envelope: AgentEventEnvelope);
}

//! Core runtime traits for execution backends, tool executors, tool registries,
//! and event sinks.
//!
//! These are the **behavioral** traits that give life to the wire-format types
//! defined in [`harness-protocol`].  The protocol crate holds only serializable
//! data structures ([`ExecutionRequest`], [`ExecutionEvent`], [`ToolCall`],
//! [`AgentEventEnvelope`], etc.); the traits here drive the actual async I/O,
//! cancellation, and streaming that implement those contracts.

use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use tokio::sync::broadcast;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_protocol::backend::{
    BackendCapabilities, BackendDescriptor, ExecutionError, ExecutionEvent, ExecutionRequest,
    ExecutionResult,
};
use harness_protocol::events::AgentEventEnvelope;
use harness_protocol::tools::{ToolCall, ToolDescriptor, ToolError, ToolResult};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ExecutionBackend
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// An execution backend that processes agent requests against a language model.
///
/// Implementations wrap a specific provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) and are
/// responsible for:
///
/// * Serializing the [`ExecutionRequest`] into the provider's wire format.
/// * Streaming back normalized [`ExecutionEvent`]s (text deltas, reasoning,
///   tool call requests, usage updates, final result, or errors).
/// * Observing the [`CancellationToken`] so that in-flight requests can be
///   aborted promptly.
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible — all methods take `&self` and return owned
/// values or futures.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ExecutionBackend: Send + Sync {
    /// Returns the backend's descriptor, including its identity and capabilities.
    fn descriptor(&self) -> BackendDescriptor;

    /// Returns a summary of the backend's capabilities.
    fn capabilities(&self) -> BackendCapabilities;

    /// Execute a request against this backend.
    ///
    /// The backend streams [`ExecutionEvent`]s into `sink` as they occur
    /// and returns the final [`ExecutionResult`] once execution completes
    /// (or an [`ExecutionError`] if something went wrong).
    ///
    /// # Cancellation
    ///
    /// When `cancel` is triggered the backend should stop work as soon as
    /// practical and return [`ExecutionError::Cancelled`].
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        request: ExecutionRequest,
        sink: broadcast::Sender<ExecutionEvent>,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult, ExecutionError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ToolExecutor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Executes a single tool call and produces a result.
///
/// Each tool (e.g. `fs.read`, `bash`, `web_search`) is represented by an
/// implementation of this trait.  Tools are stateless from the harness's
/// perspective — any state they need should be captured at construction time
/// and stored in the implementor.
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolExecutor: Send + Sync {
    /// Execute the given tool call and return its result.
    ///
    /// # Cancellation
    ///
    /// When `cancel` is triggered the tool should stop work as soon as
    /// practical and return [`ToolError::Timeout`].
    async fn execute(
        &self,
        call: ToolCall,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Result<ToolResult, ToolError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ToolRegistry
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A registry of available tool executors, indexed by tool name.
///
/// The harness uses this trait to look up tools when processing
/// [`ExecutionEvent::ToolCallRequested`] events.  Registries may be
/// session-scoped (containing only the tools granted to that session) or
/// global (containing every tool the runtime knows about).
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible.
#[async_trait]
pub trait ToolRegistry: Send + Sync {
    /// Look up a tool executor by its name (e.g. `"fs.read"`).
    ///
    /// Returns `None` if no tool with that name is registered.
    fn lookup(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn ToolExecutor>>;

    /// Returns descriptors for all registered tools.
    fn descriptors(&self) -> Vec<ToolDescriptor>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// EventSink
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A sink for receiving agent event envelopes.
///
/// Implementations are responsible for fanning events out to session-level
/// subscribers, persisting them, or forwarding them to external observers.
/// The canonical implementation publishes onto a
/// [`broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>`] but custom sinks may layer on
/// filtering, encryption, or audit logging.
///
/// # Object safety
///
/// This trait is `dyn`-compatible.
#[async_trait]
pub trait EventSink: Send + Sync {
    /// Send an event envelope for processing.
    ///
    /// Implementations **should not** block indefinitely; if the underlying
    /// channel is full the implementation should decide whether to drop the
    /// event, buffer it, or apply backpressure.
    fn send(&self, envelope: AgentEventEnvelope);
}

//! Hierarchical cancellation for agent runs (spec §35).
//!
//! Tokio's [`CancellationToken`] forms the backbone of cancellation in the
//! harness.  Each session holds a **root** [`SessionCancellation`]; every
//! agent runner, backend execution, and tool invocation derives a child token
//! from it.  Cancelling the root immediately propagates to every descendant,
//! causing in-flight work to drain promptly.

use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SessionCancellation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A hierarchical cancellation root scoped to a single session.
///
/// # Usage
///
/// ```ignore
/// let root = SessionCancellation::new();
/// let child = root.child_token();          // for one agent runner
/// let backend_token = child.child_token(); // for a backend call
///
/// // Cancel everything in the session:
/// root.cancel();
/// assert!(child.is_cancelled());
/// assert!(backend_token.is_cancelled());
/// ```
///
/// # Thread safety
///
/// All methods are lock-free and may be called from any thread.  `cancel()`
/// is idempotent — calling it multiple times has no additional effect.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct SessionCancellation {
    root: CancellationToken,
}

impl SessionCancellation {
    /// Creates a new, uncancelled root token.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            root: CancellationToken::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Returns a child token linked to the root.
    ///
    /// When the root is cancelled, all child tokens (and their descendants)
    /// are also cancelled.
    pub fn child_token(&self) -> CancellationToken {
        self.root.child_token()
    }

    /// Cancels the root token and all derived child tokens.
    ///
    /// Idempotent — subsequent calls are no-ops.
    pub fn cancel(&self) {
        self.root.cancel();
    }

    /// Returns `true` if cancellation has been requested on this root
    /// (or on any ancestor token in the hierarchy).
    pub fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool {
        self.root.is_cancelled()
    }
}

impl Default for SessionCancellation {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn new_token_is_not_cancelled() {
        let sc = SessionCancellation::new();
        assert!(!sc.is_cancelled());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancel_triggers_is_cancelled() {
        let sc = SessionCancellation::new();
        sc.cancel();
        assert!(sc.is_cancelled());
    }

    #[test]
    fn child_token_cascades_cancellation() {
        let root = SessionCancellation::new();
        let child = root.child_token();
        let grandchild = child.child_token();

        assert!(!child.is_cancelled());
        assert!(!grandchild.is_cancelled());

        root.cancel();

        assert!(child.is_cancelled());
        assert!(grandchild.is_cancelled());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancel_is_idempotent() {
        let sc = SessionCancellation::new();
        sc.cancel();
        sc.cancel(); // second call should not panic
        assert!(sc.is_cancelled());
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_is_uncancelled() {
        let sc = SessionCancellation::default();
        assert!(!sc.is_cancelled());
    }
}

//! Runtime executor that drives a single agent's lifecycle by receiving
//! [`AgentCommand`]s from its task mailbox, applying them to the agent's
//! deterministic state machine, and dispatching the resulting effects
//! to the appropriate runtime components.
//!
//! # Architecture
//!
//! ```text
//!                        ┌──────────────┐
//!   AgentCommand ───────▶│              │
//!     (from session)     │  AgentRunner │──── effect dispatch ──▶ ExecutionBackend
//!                        │              │                       ToolRegistry
//!   AgentEventEnvelope ◀─│  run() loop  │                       EventSink
//!     (to event_sink)    │              │
//!                        └──────────────┘
//! ```
//!
//! The runner is the bridge between the pure, deterministic `Agent` (from
//! `harness-core`) and the async execution infrastructure (backends, tools,
//! event sinks).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use tokio::sync::{broadcast, mpsc};
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use harness_core::agent::Agent;
use harness_protocol::backend::{ExecutionEvent, ExecutionRequest};
use harness_protocol::commands::AgentCommand;
use harness_protocol::effects::{AgentEffect, ToolRequest};
use harness_protocol::events::{AgentEvent, AgentEventEnvelope, EventVisibility};
use harness_protocol::ids::{AgentId, EventId, RunId, Timestamp, ToolCallId};

use crate::traits::{EventSink, ExecutionBackend, ToolRegistry};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentTask — mailbox for an agent
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A mailbox that connects an agent runner to the outside world.
///
/// Commands arrive via [`commands_rx`](AgentTask::commands_rx) (consumed by
/// the runner loop), while spawned tasks can inject commands through
/// [`commands_tx`](AgentTask::commands_tx).  Events are broadcast outward
/// on [`events`](AgentTask::events).
pub struct AgentTask {
    /// The agent this task belongs to.
    pub id: AgentId,

    /// Receiver side — consumed by [`AgentRunner::run`] to drive the loop.
    pub commands_rx: mpsc::Receiver<AgentCommand>,

    /// Sender side — used by spawned backend/tool tasks to report results.
    pub commands_tx: mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>,

    /// Broadcast channel for agent event envelopes (subscribed by session bus).
    pub events: broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>,
}

impl AgentTask {
    /// Create a new agent task pair with the given channel capacities.
    ///
    /// Returns the task handle alongside a broadcast receiver that the
    /// session bus can subscribe to for ordered event delivery.
    pub fn new(
        id: AgentId,
        command_capacity: usize,
        event_capacity: usize,
    ) -> (Self, broadcast::Receiver<AgentEventEnvelope>) {
        let (commands_tx, commands_rx) = mpsc::channel(command_capacity);
        let (events, event_rx) = broadcast::channel(event_capacity);
        (
            Self {
                id,
                commands_rx,
                commands_tx,
                events,
            },
            event_rx,
        )
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentRunner
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Drives a single agent's lifecycle by pulling commands from its task
/// mailbox, applying them to the deterministic [`Agent`] state machine,
/// and dispatching the resulting [`AgentEffect`]s to runtime components.
pub struct AgentRunner {
    /// The deterministic agent from `harness-core`.
    pub agent: Agent,

    /// The task mailbox (command receiver + event broadcaster).
    pub task: AgentTask,

    /// The execution backend used for LLM requests.
    pub backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,

    /// Registry of available tool executors.
    pub tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>,

    /// Sink for fully-enveloped agent events.
    pub event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink>,

    /// Monotonic agent-local event counter, incremented on every
    /// [`AgentEffect::Emit`].
    pub agent_sequence: u64,

    /// Cancellation token — a child of the session's root token.  When
    /// triggered all in-flight backend and tool work is cancelled.
    pub cancel: CancellationToken,

    // In-flight backend executions indexed by run_id (for targeted cancellation).
    backend_tokens: HashMap<RunId, CancellationToken>,

    // In-flight tool executions indexed by call_id (for targeted cancellation).
    tool_tokens: HashMap<ToolCallId, CancellationToken>,
}

impl AgentRunner {
    /// Create a new agent runner.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        agent: Agent,
        task: AgentTask,
        backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
        tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>,
        event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink>,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            agent,
            task,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            event_sink,
            agent_sequence: 0,
            cancel,
            backend_tokens: HashMap::new(),
            tool_tokens: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Public API
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Run the agent's event loop until the run finishes or the task is
    /// cancelled.
    ///
    /// This method:
    /// 1. Waits for the next [`AgentCommand`] (or cancellation signal).
    /// 2. Applies the command to the agent's state machine.
    /// 3. Dispatches each returned [`AgentEffect`].
    /// 4. Repeats until [`AgentEffect::FinishRun`] is encountered or
    ///    the agent enters a terminal state after cancellation.
    pub async fn run(&mut self) {
        loop {
            // Check for cancellation *before* waiting on the next command.
            // If cancelled, we inject Cancel into the agent and drain.
            if self.cancel.is_cancelled() && !self.is_terminal() {
                let effects = self.agent.apply(AgentCommand::Cancel);
                self.dispatch_effects(effects).await;
                // After cancellation the agent is in Cancelled state — exit.
                break;
            }

            // Wait for the next command (or for cancellation to fire).
            let command = tokio::select! {
                cmd = self.task.commands_rx.recv() => {
                    match cmd {
                        Some(c) => c,
                        None => break, // Channel closed — no more commands.
                    }
                }
                _ = self.cancel.cancelled() => {
                    // Cancellation fired while we were waiting.
                    if !self.is_terminal() {
                        let effects = self.agent.apply(AgentCommand::Cancel);
                        self.dispatch_effects(effects).await;
                    }
                    break;
                }
            };

            // Apply the command to the deterministic agent.
            let effects = self.agent.apply(command);

            // Dispatch effects — returns true if we should break.
            if self.dispatch_effects(effects).await {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Effect dispatch
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Process every effect in `effects`, dispatching to the appropriate
    /// runtime component.  Returns `true` if the runner loop should exit.
    async fn dispatch_effects(&mut self, effects: Vec<AgentEffect>) -> bool {
        let mut should_break = false;

        for effect in effects {
            match effect {
                AgentEffect::ExecuteBackend { request } => {
                    self.handle_execute_backend(request);
                }

                AgentEffect::ExecuteTool { request } => {
                    self.handle_execute_tool(request);
                }

                AgentEffect::Emit { event } => {
                    self.handle_emit(event);
                }

                AgentEffect::FinishRun { .. } => {
                    // The agent already emitted a Completed event via an Emit
                    // effect before this FinishRun.  We just need to exit.
                    should_break = true;
                }

                AgentEffect::CancelBackend { run_id } => {
                    self.handle_cancel_backend(run_id);
                }

                AgentEffect::CancelTool { call_id } => {
                    self.handle_cancel_tool(call_id);
                }

                AgentEffect::CancelChild { agent_id } => {
                    // Phase 2: stub — no child agent support yet.
                    tracing::warn!(
                        ?agent_id,
                        "AgentEffect::CancelChild: no-op in Phase 2"
                    );
                }

                AgentEffect::SpawnAgent { spec } => {
                    // Phase 2: stub — no sub-agent spawning yet.
                    tracing::warn!(
                        ?spec,
                        "AgentEffect::SpawnAgent: no-op in Phase 2"
                    );
                }

                AgentEffect::RequestPermission { request } => {
                    // Phase 2: stub — permission requests not yet wired.
                    tracing::warn!(
                        ?request,
                        "AgentEffect::RequestPermission: no-op in Phase 2"
                    );
                }

                AgentEffect::Persist { mutation } => {
                    // Phase 2: stub — persistence not yet wired.
                    tracing::warn!(
                        ?mutation,
                        "AgentEffect::Persist: no-op in Phase 2"
                    );
                }
            }
        }

        should_break
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Effect handlers
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    /// Wrap an [`AgentEvent`] in an [`AgentEventEnvelope`] and send it
    /// via the configured [`EventSink`].
    fn handle_emit(&mut self, event: AgentEvent) {
        let envelope = AgentEventEnvelope {
            event_id: EventId::new(),
            session_id: self.agent.session_id,
            agent_id: self.agent.id,
            parent_agent_id: self.agent.parent_id,
            run_id: self.agent.state.active_run,
            agent_sequence: self.agent_sequence,
            session_sequence: None,
            timestamp: Timestamp::now(),
            visibility: EventVisibility::User,
            event,
        };

        self.agent_sequence = self.agent_sequence.wrapping_add(1);
        self.event_sink.send(envelope);
    }

    /// Spawn a backend execution and forward its events back to the agent's
    /// command channel as [`AgentCommand::BackendEvent`]s.
    fn handle_execute_backend(&mut self, request: ExecutionRequest) {
        let run_id = request.run_id;
        let (event_tx, event_rx) = broadcast::channel::<ExecutionEvent>(256);

        // Create a child token for this specific backend execution so that
        // CancelBackend can target it individually.
        let backend_cancel = self.cancel.child_token();
        self.backend_tokens.insert(run_id, backend_cancel.clone());

        // --- Task 1: Drive the backend ---
        let backend = self.backend.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let _result = backend.execute(request, event_tx, backend_cancel).await;
            // When this future completes, the broadcast sender (`event_tx`) is
            // dropped, which closes the channel and causes the forwarder to exit.
        });

        // --- Task 2: Forward events to the command channel ---
        let commands_tx = self.task.commands_tx.clone();
        let cancel = self.cancel.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut rx = event_rx;
            loop {
                tokio::select! {
                    result = rx.recv() => {
                        match result {
                            Ok(event) => {
                                if commands_tx
                                    .send(AgentCommand::BackendEvent { run_id, event })
                                    .await
                                    .is_err()
                                {
                                    // Receiver dropped (runner loop ended).
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                            Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => {
                                // Backend task finished.
                                break;
                            }
                            Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(n)) => {
                                tracing::warn!(
                                    "Backend event channel lagged by {n} events (run {run_id})"
                                );
                                // Continue processing — events are still flowing.
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    _ = cancel.cancelled() => {
                        // Runner was cancelled; stop forwarding.
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }

    /// Look up the tool in the registry, spawn its execution, and forward
    /// the result back as [`AgentCommand::ToolCompleted`] or
    /// [`AgentCommand::ToolFailed`].
    fn handle_execute_tool(&mut self, request: ToolRequest) {
        let call_id = request.call.id;
        let tool_name = request.call.name.clone();
        let call = request.call;

        // Create a child token for this tool call.
        let tool_cancel = self.cancel.child_token();
        self.tool_tokens.insert(call_id, tool_cancel.clone());

        let commands_tx = self.task.commands_tx.clone();

        match self.tool_registry.lookup(&tool_name) {
            Some(executor) => {
                tokio::spawn(async move {
                    match executor.execute(call, tool_cancel).await {
                        Ok(result) => {
                            let _ = commands_tx
                                .send(AgentCommand::ToolCompleted { call_id, result })
                                .await;
                        }
                        Err(error) => {
                            let _ = commands_tx
                                .send(AgentCommand::ToolFailed { call_id, error })
                                .await;
                        }
                    }
                });
            }
            None => {
                // Tool not found — report failure immediately.
                tokio::spawn(async move {
                    let _ = commands_tx
                        .send(AgentCommand::ToolFailed {
                            call_id,
                            error: harness_protocol::tools::ToolError::ExecutionFailed,
                        })
                        .await;
                });
            }
        }
    }

    /// Cancel a specific backend execution by triggering its child token.
    fn handle_cancel_backend(&mut self, run_id: RunId) {
        if let Some(token) = self.backend_tokens.remove(&run_id) {
            token.cancel();
        }
    }

    /// Cancel a specific tool execution by triggering its child token.
    fn handle_cancel_tool(&mut self, call_id: ToolCallId) {
        if let Some(token) = self.tool_tokens.remove(&call_id) {
            token.cancel();
        }
    }

    /// Returns `true` if the agent is in a terminal state where no further
    /// commands should be processed.
    fn is_terminal(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self.agent.state.status,
            harness_protocol::commands::AgentStatus::Cancelled
                | harness_protocol::commands::AgentStatus::Completed
                | harness_protocol::commands::AgentStatus::Failed
        )
    }
}

/// Aggregates event broadcasts from all agent runners in a session and fans
/// them out to external subscribers as a single ordered stream.
///
/// # Ordering
///
/// Every event that flows through the bus receives a monotonically increasing
/// [`session_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::session_sequence) number.  This,
/// combined with the agent-local [`agent_sequence`](AgentEventEnvelope::agent_sequence),
/// allows consumers to reconstruct a total order across all agents in the
/// session.
///
/// # Lifecycle
///
/// 1. Create with [`SessionEventBus::new`].
/// 2. As each agent runner is spawned, call
///    [`register_agent`](SessionEventBus::register_agent) with the broadcast
///    sender from that runner's [`AgentTask`].
/// 3. Spawn the [`run`](SessionEventBus::run) loop as a background tokio task.
/// 4. External consumers obtain a receiver via
///    [`subscribe`](SessionEventBus::subscribe).
pub struct SessionEventBus {
    /// Broadcast receivers for each registered agent. Wrapped in a [`Mutex`]
    /// so that agents can be registered from any thread while the run loop
    /// polls them concurrently.
    receivers: Mutex<Vec<broadcast::Receiver<AgentEventEnvelope>>>,

    /// Shared sender for external subscribers carved from the broadcast
    /// channel created in [`new`](SessionEventBus::new).
    subscriber_sender: broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>,

    /// Monotonically increasing session-level sequence counter. Every event
    /// that flows through the bus receives the next value before being fanned
    /// out.
    session_sequence: AtomicU64,
}

impl SessionEventBus {
    /// Create a new event bus with the given subscriber channel capacity.
    pub fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let (subscriber_sender, _) = broadcast::channel(capacity);
        Self {
            receivers: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
            subscriber_sender,
            session_sequence: AtomicU64::new(0),
        }
    }

    /// Register a new agent's event source with the bus.
    ///
    /// The `sender` should be the [`broadcast::Sender`] from the agent's
    /// [`AgentTask::events`]. The bus creates a receiver and will poll it
    /// in the [`run`](SessionEventBus::run) loop.
    pub fn register_agent(
        &self,
        _agent_id: AgentId,
        sender: broadcast::Sender<AgentEventEnvelope>,
    ) {
        let rx = sender.subscribe();
        self.receivers
            .lock()
            .expect("receivers mutex poisoned")
            .push(rx);
    }

    /// Return a new subscriber receiver that will receive all session events.
    pub fn subscribe(&self) -> broadcast::Receiver<AgentEventEnvelope> {
        self.subscriber_sender.subscribe()
    }

    /// Run the event bus's forwarding loop.
    ///
    /// Polls every registered agent receiver via [`try_recv`],
    /// assigns a monotonically increasing `session_sequence` to each event,
    /// and forwards to all subscribers.  Exits when `bus_cancel` is
    /// triggered.
    pub async fn run(&self, bus_cancel: CancellationToken) {
        loop {
            if bus_cancel.is_cancelled() {
                break;
            }

            let mut had_data = false;

            let mut receivers = self
                .receivers
                .lock()
                .expect("receivers mutex poisoned");

            receivers.retain_mut(|rx| loop {
                match rx.try_recv() {
                    Ok(mut envelope) => {
                        let seq =
                            self.session_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        envelope.session_sequence = Some(seq);
                        let _ = self.subscriber_sender.send(envelope);
                        had_data = true;
                    }
                    Err(broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Empty) => break,
                    Err(broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Closed) => return false,
                    Err(broadcast::error::TryRecvError::Lagged(n)) => {
                        tracing::warn!("Session event bus lagged by {n} events");
                    }
                }
            });

            drop(receivers);

            if !had_data {
                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
            } else {
                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
            }
        }
    }
}

            .expect("Completed event");

    }

//!
//! This module provides three primary types:
//!
//! * [`SessionBuilder`] — a fluent builder for configuring and starting
//!   sessions.

use std::sync::Arc;

use tokio::sync::broadcast;

use harness_protocol::ids::SessionId;

/// Errors that can occur during session construction or operation.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum HarnessError {
    /// The `backend` field was not set before calling [`SessionBuilder::start`].
    #[error("missing required field: backend")]
    MissingBackend,

    /// The `tools` (tool_registry) field was not set before calling
    /// [`SessionBuilder::start`].
    #[error("missing required field: tool_registry")]
    MissingToolRegistry,

    /// A session‑level runtime error occurred (e.g. invalid state, cancelled).
    #[error("session error: {0}")]
    Session(#[from] SessionError),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A fluent builder for creating and starting harness sessions.
///
/// ## Example
///
/// ```ignore
/// let handle = Harness::new()
///     .session()
///     .backend(backend)
///     .tools(tool_registry)
///     .start()
///     .await?;
/// ```
pub struct SessionBuilder {
    /// The execution backend to use for this session.
    backend: Option<Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>>,
    /// The tool registry to use for this session.
    tool_registry: Option<Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>>,
}

impl SessionBuilder {
    /// Create a new, empty [`SessionBuilder`].
    ///
    /// All fields are initially `None` and must be set via the builder
    /// methods before calling [`start()`](SessionBuilder::start).
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            backend: None,
            tool_registry: None,
        }
    }

    /// Set the execution backend for this session.
    ///
    /// This is required — [`start()`](SessionBuilder::start) will return
    /// [`HarnessError::MissingBackend`] if this is not set.
    pub fn backend(mut self, backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>) -> Self {
        self.backend = Some(backend);
        self
    }

    /// Set the tool registry for this session.
    ///
    /// This is required — [`start()`](SessionBuilder::start) will return
    /// [`HarnessError::MissingToolRegistry`] if this is not set.
    pub fn tools(mut self, tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>) -> Self {
        self.tool_registry = Some(tool_registry);
        self
    }

    /// Consume the builder and start a new session.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`HarnessError::MissingBackend`] if
    /// [`backend()`](SessionBuilder::backend) was not called.
    ///
    /// Returns [`HarnessError::MissingToolRegistry`] if
    /// [`tools()`](SessionBuilder::tools) was not called.
    pub async fn start(self) -> Result<SessionHandle, HarnessError> {
        let backend = self
            .backend
            .ok_or(HarnessError::MissingBackend)?;
        let tool_registry = self
            .tool_registry
            .ok_or(HarnessError::MissingToolRegistry)?;

        let session_id = SessionId::new();

        // Create a broadcast channel for session events.
        // Capacity 256 is a reasonable default — the broadcast channel
        // is used for event fan-out to subscribers.
        let (event_tx, _) = broadcast::channel::<AgentEventEnvelope>(256);

        // Construct the session runtime with the provided backend,
        // tool registry, and event bus.
        let runtime = Arc::new(SessionRuntime::new(
            session_id,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            event_tx,
        ));

        // Create the session client that wraps the runtime.
        let client = SessionClient::new(runtime);

        Ok(SessionHandle {
            client,
            session_id,
        })
    }
}
